subject: Topology attestation & segregation workplan for Private/Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@valencia-health.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: security@valencia-health.com
Date: 2027-07-07T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Topology attestation for Private Dedicated deployment

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our procurement/security review we need a brief attestation and supporting artifacts for the proposed Private/Dedicated deployment model. Specifically Valencia needs: 

- A single-page network topology (logical) showing control-plane vs data-plane boundaries and any bridge/egress points to customer VPCs or on-prem networks.
- A short statement describing tenant isolation guarantees (how we prevent cross-tenant traffic, ACLs/VLANs used, and KV/cache separation).
- Egress control explanation (NAT/Egress gateways, allowlist/denylist patterns) and where KMS keys are scoped.
- Pointer to SOC 2 evidence and a filled CAIQ/SIG mapping if available.

We aim to present this to our internal Risk Board next week (target review: 2027-07-12). Can you share the attestation and any supporting diagrams or playbooks? A PDF + a vector diagram would be ideal.

If useful, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the diagram.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Senior Security Engineer — Valencia Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@valencia-health.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Topology attestation for Private Dedicated deployment

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching an initial attestation package and a compact topology diagram for your Risk Board. Attachments in this email: "segregation-bridge_v1.svg" (logical topology) and "isolation-playbook_v1.pdf" (2-page playbook + control statements).

Summary of what we've included in the attestation:
- Control-plane separation: customer control-plane APIs are hosted in a logically separate cluster pool; we use mTLS between control components and the data-plane hosts. No direct tenant data persists on control-plane nodes.
- Data-plane tenant fencing: tenants are placed into isolated compute pools; network-level isolation uses per-tenant VXLAN segments combined with strict host-based iptables rules to prevent lateral movement.
- KV cache and model state: per-tenant cache namespaces; encryption-at-rest using customer-scoped CMKs when requested; default CMK per-region otherwise.
- Egress gating: egress flows originate from per-pool NAT gateways with centralized allowlist rules maintained in our policy service. Sensitive telemetry and model checkpoint upload paths are forced through an encrypted egress gateway and logged.

Open questions for your Risk Board (so we can tailor evidence):
1) Do you require customer-managed KMS (HSM) or is customer-scoped CMK OK?
2) Will you need runbooks for tenant evictions / incident-derived segmentation actions?
3) Any particular SIG/CAT questions we should map first?

Next steps we propose:
- Kimberly will add the network control-plane egress matrix (CSV) with port/IP mappings.
- Karthik will attach SOC 2 artifact pointers and a high-level CAIQ mapping.
- We can schedule a review call — propose 2027-07-08 or 2027-07-09.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@valencia-health.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-07T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Topology attestation for Private Dedicated deployment

Elena / team — adding a few technical asserts and an attachment (controlplane-egress-matrix.csv) with the ports and IP ranges we expect to use. Quoting Neha below for context: 

> - Control-plane separation: customer control-plane APIs are hosted in a logically separate cluster pool; we use mTLS between control components and the data-plane hosts. No direct tenant data persists on control-plane nodes.

Notes and clarifications (short):
- VLAN/VXLAN: We use per-tenant VXLAN IDs tied to an internal orchestration policy; overlay termination happens at hypervisor/router boundary in the tenant compute cluster. This prevents cross-tenant L2 adjacency.
- Host firewall: Default-deny iptables at the host; orchestration injects ephemeral allow rules for scheduled job windows.
- KV and cache: Redis namespaces are process-isolated and run on dedicated instances for Dedicated customers; we enforce RBAC on management endpoints.
- Sidecar and kernel hardening: Sidecar enforces TLS + token-based auth for intra-host RPCs and drops non-auth flows. We also apply seccomp profiles for inference binaries in Dedicated pools.
- Egress auditing: All egress is NATed through a small set of audited egress gateways; we retain flow logs for 90 days by default and can extend to 365 days for enterprise contracts.

Attachment: controlplane-egress-matrix.csv (port, protocol, source CIDR, destination, purpose).

I'll be on the call proposed by Neha; happy to walk through the bridging points where customer VPC peering or VPNs are involved.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Infrastructure Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@valencia-health.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Topology attestation for Private Dedicated deployment

Neha / Kimberly — received, and thank you. The materials look promising. A few quick asks from Risk before we close: 

- Can you provide the SOC 2 control IDs and corresponding artifact names (even a short lookup table) so our auditors can reference them quickly?
- Please add a one-line statement on how tenant KV namespaces are destroyed/rotated when a customer terminates their Dedicated instance.
- We would like the CAIQ/SIG mapping for the first review; if you have a partially-completed mapping, that will work — we just need the rows covering network zoning, key management, and tenant isolation.

If you can drop these into the Drive folder (link below) by EOD 2027-07-12 we can proceed with the Risk Board review the following week. Otherwise let's lock a 30-min walkthrough on 2027-07-13.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleLinkRedwoodValencia

Elena
